## TL;DR

Both `repoos message` and `repoos send-back` now accept inline text, stdin, file options and `--message` through a shared parser. Invalid or ambiguous input is rejected before contacting the server, and successful human-readable output identifies the message length and first line.

## Work and rationale

The incident arose because the message command joined every remaining argument as text. A dash or an unrecognized file flag could therefore become a successful but useless instruction. Send-back had a separate, narrower parser. The shared parser makes the same input forms available to both commands and checks for unknown flags, missing option values, conflicting sources, empty content, unreadable files and terminal stdin before creating an API client. It preserves the existing trimming behavior and supports `--message-file -` as well as a positional dash and implicit piped stdin. JSON output remains machine-readable as before.

The non-JSON success messages include the character count and first line for queued, immediate and ordinary delivery, and for send-back. Help and the CLI guide describe the new forms. The existing AGENTS.md references do not describe the old input behavior, so they need no correction.

Table-driven tests run the input forms against each command, check the outgoing API payload, and verify that malformed inputs never reach the API. They also check the visible success summary. The existing integration tests remain useful for the actual server sequence.

## Approaches tried

I inspected the existing common flag parser and send-back file reader. A dedicated shared message parser avoids interpreting a message option's value as a common flag, while retaining the same file and stdin reading mechanism. I inspected other joined arguments and stdin handling: the other server-backed join is a config value, and task notes are local activity entries; changing their interface would exceed this task's scope.

## Challenges and blockers

A missing positional message must distinguish a terminal from redirected stdin without blocking an interactive session. The parser checks terminal status before reading and rejects an empty result in either case. It also rejects combinations before any server call. No external accounts or human steps were required.

## Key learnings

Free-text command arguments need explicit source selection and validation before a success can be reported. Showing a small description of the actual payload provides a useful second check while retaining JSON output for automation.
